patchedVersion: No patched version published in official advisory at review time
dependency: Transitive development dependency through eslint-config-next -> @next/eslint-plugin-next -> fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces
productionAbsenceBasis: Exact standalone image inventory, failed module resolutions, full /app JS/JSON token scan and manual review of all3 lexical-hit files; production audit0 supports but does not establish absence alone.
productionAbsenceLimit: Scoped component/package finding, not a universal proof of every unlabeled code fragment or of Picomatch safety.
vulnerableMechanism: Deep attacker-controlled nested glob patterns drive recursive AST walking and exhaust the JavaScript call stack.
developmentReachability: Vulnerable code present in developer/lint glob chain. No runtime endpoint takes glob patterns. Current lint configuration is versioned and repository-defined, but an untrusted checkout/PR or changed glob configuration can feed pathological patterns; development dependency is not harmless by definition.
existingMitigations: Reviewed rehearsal uses trusted local checkout with fixed lint/configuration patterns.
No braces package in inspected traced standalone production output.
Registry integrity and lockfile pinning improve identity; they do not cure the recursion vulnerability.
proposedOperationalConditionsNotEnforced: Keep affected developer tooling restricted to reviewed local checkouts; do not feed attacker-controlled nested glob patterns.

Run any untrusted branch/tooling in disposable least-privileged environments without real data, deployment credentials or mounted sensitive host resources; no new isolation workflow has been implemented.
Stop and reassess if advisory provides fix, dependency/runtime scope changes, or a tool failure exposes reachable untrusted pattern input.
recommendedDisposition: Retain OPEN / NO FIX AVAILABLE with documented bounded tooling controls and explicit independent owner acknowledgement; do not mark CLOSED, bundle into OS R20 approval, suppress the finding, or upgrade without authorization.
